implemented.title: Retry with backoff on CISA KEV and EPSS fetch failures
implemented.description: fetch_kev() and fetch_epss() previously made a single bare HTTP attempt each, unlike nvd_query() which already retried 3x with exponential backoff. A transient network blip, 429, or 5xx from either CISA KEV or FIRST.org EPSS would silently zero out KEV status (losing the +25 risk-score bonus for every alert that run) or EPSS scores (40% of the composite risk score) for the whole run, degrading risk-score accuracy without any visible failure. Both functions now use the same 3-attempt exponential backoff pattern already established for NVD, with explicit stderr logging of each retry attempt. Zero new dependencies, zero new API calls under normal conditions (retries only fire on actual failure).

implemented.title: Retry with backoff on Dependabot Alerts API pagination fetch
implemented.description: fetch_dependabot_alerts() was the last remaining HTTP call in the pipeline still making a single bare attempt per page. Added 3-attempt exponential backoff on 429/5xx/transient errors.

implemented.title: Retry with backoff on GHSA advisories fetch
implemented.description: fetch_ghsa_advisories() was the last remaining external HTTP call without retry. Added the identical 429/5xx-retried pattern used everywhere else in the file.

implemented.title: Frontend accessibility: labels and aria-attributes on filter controls
implemented.description: Added visually-hidden labels, aria-label attributes, aria-live result count, role=status empty-state, and aria-expanded on the score-breakdown toggle. Pure additive markup, zero visual change.

implemented.title: Retry with backoff on GitHub Issue creation (notify_github_issues.py)
implemented.description: create_issue() was the last remaining external HTTP call in the entire pipeline without retry. Added the identical 429/5xx-retried pattern, closing the reliability layer across both aggregate.py and notify_github_issues.py.

implemented.title: Refresh EPSS/KEV/risk_score for existing alerts outside NVD lookback window
implemented.description: Previously, once a CVE aged out of the NVD lookback window (2 days in production CI, 8 days default locally) or wasn't resurfaced by Dependabot/GHSA that run, its epss_score (40% of composite risk_score) and kev status froze permanently at the value captured on first_seen -- even though FIRST.org publishes new EPSS scores daily and CISA KEV catalog additions are unrelated to NVD's lastModified window. Now every run also queries EPSS/KEV for all existing tracked alerts (not just ones resurfaced this cycle) and refreshes epss_score, epss_percentile, kev, kev_date_added, kev_due_date, kev_ransomware_use, kev_required_action, risk_score, and risk_score_breakdown in place for the untouched ones -- leaving description/cvss_score/source/first_seen/affected fields alone since this run has no fresher data for them. Validated locally: same 438 CVEs before/after, first_seen and cvss_score untouched, only score fields updated; EPSS query volume rose from ~305 (filtered-only) to ~943 (all 438 tracked + new candidates, deduplicated) CVEs, still a single unauthenticated batched FIRST.org endpoint call (no key, generous free rate limit), well within zero-cost constraints. Live CI run hit transient NVD 503s (existing retry logic absorbed them, non-fatal) and completed successfully with correct output.

implemented.title: Shareable filter state via URL query params
implemented.description: Dashboard filters (search, KEV status, source, sort order) previously reset on every page load and could not be shared or bookmarked -- e.g. a security lead could not send a teammate a direct link to 'KEV overdue only, sorted by risk score'. Added readFiltersFromURL() (reads q/kev/source/sort from location.search on load, no-op for unrecognized values since setting a <select>.value to a nonexistent option is a browser no-op) and updateURLFromFilters() (writes the current filter state into the URL via history.replaceState on every applyFiltersAndRender call, so it never spams browser history and defaults are omitted from the URL to keep links clean). Zero backend/API changes, zero new dependencies, purely additive client-side JS. Scored 5/5/5: zero cost, low validation risk (pure URL<->DOM sync, no data mutation), real value (shareable/bookmarkable triage views, a genuine UX gap for a security-team tool).

implemented.title: Show watchlist keyword-match badges on alert cards
implemented.description: The aggregate.py pipeline has captured matched_keywords (which watchlist.yaml keyword term(s) caused a CVE to surface, e.g. 'wordpress') per alert since early cycles, and 129/438 currently-tracked alerts have a non-empty value -- but the field was never rendered on the dashboard, so a security lead reviewing the feed had no visual indicator of WHY a given CVE was flagged as relevant versus appearing from a generic NVD/GHSA/Dependabot sweep. Added a small green 'Watchlist match' badge row per matched keyword to renderCard() in docs/app.js (purely additive DOM, no new fields/API calls) and matching .matched/.badge.match CSS rules in docs/style.css. Renders only when matched_keywords is non-empty; alerts with an empty array (majority, from generic source-driven presence) are unaffected.

implemented.title: Stale-data warning banner on dashboard
implemented.description:
The aggregation pipeline runs on a 4-hour GitHub Actions schedule but the public dashboard had no way to signal if it silently stopped updating (broken workflow, disabled schedule cron, repeated failures) -- a security lead would keep trusting increasingly-old data indefinitely with zero visual cue. Added checkStaleness() in docs/app.js, called from the existing loadStats() fetch of data/stats.json: compares stats.generated_at against Date.now() and, if the gap exceeds 20 hours (5x the 4h cadence, tolerant of one missed/delayed run without false-alarming on normal Actions scheduling jitter), shows a visible red role=alert banner naming the exact staleness age in hours and pointing the viewer to check GitHub Actions. Pure additive frontend change: new #stale-banner

element in docs/index.html (hidden by default), a new .stale-banner CSS rule in docs/style.css, and the checkStaleness() function plus one call site in docs/app.js. Zero new API calls, zero backend/schema changes, zero risk to existing data pipeline.

implemented.title: Add 'View on NVD' direct link to alert cards
implemented.description: Every alert card already showed source/CVSS/EPSS/risk data and (for Dependabot-sourced alerts) a link to the GitHub Dependabot alert, but a viewer wanting the canonical NVD record for a CVE (full CVSS vector, references, CPE match strings, CWE classification) had to manually construct or search for the URL themselves -- a real friction point for a security-team triage tool where NVD is the authoritative source. Added a 'View on NVD' link (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/<cve_id>) to the card footer for every alert whose cve_id matches the CVE- prefix pattern (all of them in current data), placed alongside the existing Dependabot alert link inside a new .footer-links flex wrapper. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Mobile-responsive @media breakpoint (max-width: 600px)
implemented.description: The dashboard had a viewport meta tag but zero @media rules in style.css, so narrow-screen visitors got desktop sizing squeezed into a small column: toolbar controls row overflowing/wrapping awkwardly, dep-filter textarea forced to a 240px min-width wider than many phones, count text floating far right of a wrapped controls line. Added a single 600px breakpoint that stacks toolbar controls to full width, switches card-grid to single column, drops the textarea min-width constraint, and tightens header/main padding. Pure additive CSS, zero visual change above 600px (verified: desktop screenshot before/after identical). Validated locally at 375x812 (iPhone-class viewport) via the browser tool: confirmed no horizontal overflow (document.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth), controls/textarea/card-grid render correctly stacked. Live-verified on the production dashboard at the same viewport: stats bar, historical trend chart, and dependency filter section all render correctly stacked with no overflow.

implemented.title: SEO meta tags, Open Graph/Twitter cards, inline SVG favicon
implemented.description: The dashboard's <head> had zero meta description, no Open Graph/Twitter card tags for link previews, and requested /favicon.ico which 404'd (confirmed via curl before the change). Added: a meta description summarizing the tool for search engines; og:title/og:description/og:type/og:url and twitter:card/twitter:title/twitter:description for rich link previews when the dashboard URL is shared (Slack, Twitter/X, Discord, etc. -- relevant for a security-team tool that gets shared in incident channels); and a data-URI inline SVG favicon (shield-with-checkmark icon in the dashboard's own color palette) so the browser tab/bookmark no longer 404s on every load, adding zero external asset requests. Pure additive HTML <head> change: 9 lines added to docs/index.html, zero JS/CSS/backend/schema changes, zero new API calls, zero cost.

implemented.title: Per-CVE shareable deep-link with click-to-copy and scroll-to-highlight
implemented.description: Each alert card already had a unique cve_id but no way to link directly to a single specific card -- only the whole filtered view was shareable (cycle 7's URL query params). Added: (1) each card now gets id="alert-<CVE-ID>" and its CVE-ID span became a clickable <button class=cve-link-btn> that copies a #alert-<CVE-ID> deep-link to the clipboard (navigator.clipboard.writeText, with a graceful no-op fallback if clipboard API is unavailable) and shows a transient 'Copied!' label; (2) a new highlightFromHash() function runs on every loadData() completion, checking location.hash for #alert-<CVE-ID>, scrolling that card into view (scrollIntoView smooth/center) and adding a temporary .highlighted CSS class (blue glow border, auto-removed after 2.5s) if the card exists in the current dataset -- fails silently if not found (e.g. filtered out or not yet ingested). Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost. Validated locally on scratch port (438/440-alert real production data): confirmed click-to-copy sets the URL hash and clipboard content, confirmed a fresh page load with #alert-<CVE-ID> in the URL correctly scrolls to and highlights that exact card (verified via a genuine new_tab navigation -- an in-page goto_url hash-only change does not re-fire the full load path, which was a test-methodology artifact, not a bug, confirmed by testing with real navigation). Confirmed zero regression to existing search filter and risk-score breakdown toggle. Live-verified on production: cve-link-btn renders correctly on the live dashboard.

implemented.title: Days-overdue count on KEV OVERDUE badge
implemented.description: The existing OVERDUE badge (from cycle-1-era KEV due-date tracking) told the viewer a CVE had passed its CISA KEV BOD 22-01 remediation due date, but gave no magnitude -- a badge that's 1 day overdue and one that's 90 days overdue looked identical, which matters for a security team's triage priority (a compliance deadline missed by 90 days is a materially different escalation than 1 day). Added overdueDays(alert) in docs/app.js (pure function: computes whole days between kev_due_date and now, returns null if not overdue -- reuses the existing isOverdue() decision logic unchanged, just adds a magnitude on top) and updated the OVERDUE badge template to render e.g. 'OVERDUE (12d)'. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Show alert count by source (stats.by_source) breakdown pills on dashboard
implemented.description: compute_stats() in aggregate.py has computed a by_source dict (e.g. {"nvd": 440}) since early cycles, but it was never rendered on the dashboard -- a viewer had no quick way to see the source mix (NVD sweep vs GHSA vs Dependabot contributions) without exporting CSV and counting manually. Added renderSourceBreakdown() to docs/app.js, called from the existing loadStats() fetch of data/stats.json: renders one small pill per source (name + count, sorted by count descending) into a new #source-breakdown div in docs/index.html, hidden when by_source is empty/missing. Added matching .source-breakdown/.source-pill CSS rules to docs/style.css. Pure additive frontend change reading an existing stats.json field: zero new API calls, zero backend/schema changes, zero cost. Validated locally on scratch port 8817 with real production data (440 alerts): node --check passed, pill rendered correctly as 'nvd: 440', confirmed zero regression to stats bar, historical trend chart, and search filter (wordpress query still correctly narrowed 440->125). Live-verified on production: curl confirmed new identifiers present in deployed app.js/index.html, and a live browser load confirmed the #source-breakdown div is populated with 'nvd: 440' and the result count still reads 440 of 440 alerts.

implemented.title: DUE SOON badge for KEV entries within 7 days of remediation deadline
implemented.description: Cycle 14 added a days-overdue magnitude to the existing OVERDUE badge, but there was no forward-looking equivalent -- a KEV entry due in 2 days looked identical to one due in 60 days until it actually crossed the deadline and became OVERDUE, giving a security team zero advance warning to prioritize remediation before a BOD 22-01 compliance breach. Added daysUntilDue(alert) to docs/app.js (mutually exclusive with the existing overdueDays()/isOverdue(): returns null if there's no due date or the date has already passed) and a new yellow 'DUE SOON (Nd)' badge rendered on renderCard() whenever 0 <= days-until-due <= 7, alongside the existing KEV/RANSOMWARE/OVERDUE badges. Added matching .badge.due-soon CSS rule to docs/style.css. Pure additive frontend change reading the existing kev_due_date field: zero new API calls, zero backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Add 'KEV due soon (<=7d)' filter option to dashboard
implemented.description: Cycle 16 added a DUE SOON badge (0-7 days until CISA KEV BOD 22-01 remediation deadline) but there was no way to isolate just those alerts in the existing KEV-status filter dropdown -- a security lead had to scan every card visually to find upcoming deadlines. Added a 'KEV due soon (<=7d) only' option to the #kev-filter <select> in docs/index.html, and matching filter logic in applyFiltersAndRender() in docs/app.js reusing the existing daysUntilDue() helper from cycle 16 (0 <= days <= 7). Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost. Composes with the existing URL-query-param sharing (cycle 7) so a filtered 'due soon' view is itself shareable/bookmarkable.

implemented.title: Add 'KEV due date (soonest first)' sort option
implemented.description: Added a new sort option to the existing #sort-by dropdown that orders cards by kev_due_date ascending (soonest CISA KEV BOD 22-01 remediation deadline first). Non-KEV alerts and KEV entries with no published due date are pushed to the end (not the front, avoiding the classic empty-string-sorts-first bug) rather than being treated as most urgent. Complements cycle 16's DUE SOON badge and cycle 17's 'KEV due soon' filter -- together a security lead can now filter to due-soon KEV entries AND sort the whole board by proximity to deadline, composing for free with the existing URL-query-param sharing (writes ?sort=kev_due_date).

implemented.title: Add 'First seen' age badge and 'Oldest first' triage-backlog sort
implemented.description: Every alert card already showed 'Published' (vendor/NVD publish date) but had no way to answer 'how long has our team known about this' -- a distinct triage-aging question, since first_seen (set once on first ingestion, never touched by score-refresh cycles) can differ from Published by years for old CVEs that only start matching the watchlist later. Added a firstSeenAge() helper computing whole days since first_seen, rendered as a small 'First seen: Nd ago' badge in the card footer, plus a new 'Sort: Oldest first (triage backlog)' option in the existing #sort-by dropdown so a security lead can surface long-lingering un-triaged alerts that the default newest-first sort keeps pushing off-screen. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes (first_seen already existed in alerts.json), zero cost. Adjusted .card-footer CSS to flex-wrap with gap since it now holds 3 elements instead of 2.

implemented.title: Add severity (CVSS band) filter dropdown
implemented.description: severityClass() has computed critical/high/medium/low CVSS bands since early cycles (used for card border color) but there was no way to filter the board by severity band -- only KEV status and source had dropdowns. Added a #severity-filter <select> to docs/index.html (all/critical/high/medium/low, mirroring the existing severityClass() thresholds: >=9, 7-8.9, 4-6.9, <4) and matching filter logic in applyFiltersAndRender() in docs/app.js, reusing the existing severityClass() helper unchanged. Composes with the existing URL-query-param sharing (cycle 7) via a new sev= param, so a filtered severity view is itself shareable/bookmarkable, and with the dependency-file filter and search. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Redistribute risk-score weight when CVSS or EPSS is missing (instead of scoring as zero)
implemented.description: composite_risk_score() previously treated a missing CVSS or EPSS value as 0, i.e. silently asserting definite-low-severity/definite-low-exploitability for a CVE that simply has not been scored yet by NVD/FIRST.org -- 112/445 currently-tracked alerts are missing epss_score. Now each present component (CVSS 35%, EPSS 40%, KEV flat 25%) has its weight redistributed proportionally across whatever components ARE known, so a partial-data CVE risk_score reflects only real signal rather than being artificially deflated. risk_score_breakdown gained a weight_redistributed boolean and per-component effective-weight strings (e.g. "58.3% of (CVSS/10)" when EPSS is missing); the dashboard breakdown panel renders these plus a new explanatory note when redistribution occurred, and the footer methodology text documents the behavior. Pure risk-scoring-accuracy + transparency fix: no new API calls, no new external data sources, one new boolean field on an already-present nested object.

implemented.title: Debounce search input (150ms)
implemented.description: The dashboard search box previously triggered a full filter+sort+innerHTML re-render of the card grid (plus a history.replaceState URL sync from cycle 7's shareable-filters feature) on every single keystroke. With 445+ alerts and growing over time, typing a multi-character search term fired repeated full-grid rebuilds for every intermediate substring the user never intended to search for -- wasted CPU work and, on lower-end/mobile devices, visible input lag as the alert count grows. Wrapped the existing search input listener in a 150ms debounce (setTimeout/clearTimeout pattern, well under common UX guidance of ~100-300ms for search-as-you-type to still feel instant), collapsing rapid keystrokes into a single render after the user pauses typing. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost. Validated: node --check passed; served docs/ on a scratch local port with real production data (445 alerts), confirmed via browser tool that typing 'chrome' left the result count unchanged at 445/445 immediately after the keystroke event fired (debounce delaying execution) and correctly updated to 56/445 after ~400ms; confirmed clearing search correctly resets to 445/445 and the stats bar still renders correctly (101 critical, 1 KEV, 0.8% avg EPSS). No aggregate.py/data changes so no GitHub Actions data-pipeline run was needed; live-verified by polling the GitHub Pages build deployment run to completion, curling https://astruzocyber.github.io/CVE/app.js to confirm the new searchDebounceTimer code is live (200 OK, code present), and loading the live production dashboard in the browser tool -- screenshot confirmed correct rendering (stats bar, historical trend chart, KEV/critical counts all intact, no regression).

implemented.title: Extract and display CWE/weakness classification
implemented.description: NVD's weaknesses array, GHSA's advisory.cwes, and Dependabot's advisory.cwes were already present in API responses already being fetched (no new API calls) but never parsed. Added extract_cwe_ids() helpers wired into all three source parsers (NVD, GHSA, Dependabot) and propagated cwe_ids (list of CWE-NNN strings) into the final entry schema. Frontend renders a new .cwe-row of linked badges (each links to cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/<N>.html) below the Affected line on every card, and cwe_ids was added as a column to the CSV export. Pure additive data enrichment: zero new network calls, zero new rate-limit risk. Validated: ast.parse/node --check passed; ran aggregate.py for real against production data (477 alerts processed, 342 populated cwe_ids, 135 pre-existing untouched alerts correctly lack the key until their next refresh -- same expected behavior as any newly-added field), then git checkout'd the throwaway local data files before commit so real production data was untouched. Frontend validated via a local scratch HTTP server with synthetic CWE-79/CWE-352 test values, confirming correct badge/link DOM structure. Live-verified: pushed, triggered cve-alerts.yml (completed success, 1m37s, no new warnings/errors beyond known-benign Node 20 deprecation noise), pulled the freshly-regenerated live data (500 alerts, 250 with cwe_ids), curled all four changed live URLs (200 OK), and loaded the live dashboard in the browser tool confirming a real card (CVE-2026-85046) renders a correct CWE-843 badge/link, plus stats bar and search/filter UI unaffected (500 cards, stats populated).

implemented.title: Add one-click 'Reset filters' button
implemented.description: The dashboard had 5 independent filter/sort controls (search, KEV status, severity, source, sort-by) plus a client-side dependency-file filter, but no single way to clear all of them at once -- a viewer who had stacked several filters (e.g. search + KEV-only + severity + pasted package.json) had to reset each control individually. Added a Reset filters button next to Export CSV in docs/index.html, wired in docs/app.js to blank the search box, set every select back to its default option, clear dependencyPackageNames plus the dep-text-input/dep-file-input/dep-status DOM, and re-render -- reusing the existing applyFiltersAndRender()/updateURLFromFilters() path so the shareable-URL query params (cycle 7) are cleared too. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost. Validated: node --check passed; served docs/ on a scratch local port with real production data (500 alerts), used the browser tool to stack a search term + KEV-only filter (110->1 of 500), clicked Reset, confirmed all controls reverted to default, result count returned to 500 of 500, and the URL query string was cleared. Live-verified on production: curled app.js/index.html (200 OK, reset-filters string present), loaded the live dashboard, applied a search filter (500->0 of 500 for a nonsense scoped test), clicked Reset, confirmed it correctly returned to 500 of 500.

implemented.title: Include CWE IDs in search haystack
implemented.description: CWE badges have been rendered on alert cards since cycle 23 (extract_cwe_ids feature), but the search box haystack in applyFiltersAndRender() only indexed cve_id, description, affected, and matched_keywords -- cwe_ids was never added, so a viewer typing e.g. "CWE-79" to find all XSS-classified CVEs got zero results despite the CWE-79 badge being visibly present on matching cards. Added cwe_ids (spread into the existing haystack array) so free-text search now matches on CWE ID. Pure additive one-line client-side change, no new API calls, no backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Optional 'Total tracked alerts' line on historical trend chart
implemented.description: docs/data/history/trend.csv has recorded total_alerts (column 2) every run since cycle-1-era history tracking began, but the Chart.js trend chart only ever plotted kev_overdue_count and avg_epss -- the raw alert-volume growth trend (a meaningful signal for a security lead: 'is our watchlist/data coverage growing steadily or did something break/spike?') was invisible even though the data was already being fetched and rendered as the x-axis labels source. Added a third dataset ('Total tracked alerts', parsed from the already-fetched trend.csv column 1) on a new hidden y2 axis (display:false, so it doesn't visually compete with the two existing labeled axes), defaulted to hidden:true in the Chart.js dataset config so the default view is byte-for-byte visually identical to before -- a viewer opts in by clicking the legend item, standard Chart.js interaction pattern. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes (total_alerts already existed as trend.csv column 2), zero cost.

implemented.title: Render CISA KEV 'required action' guidance on alert cards
implemented.description: CISA's KEV catalog API has always returned a requiredAction field per entry (the specific remediation guidance CISA publishes for that KEV CVE) and aggregate.py has captured it into kev_required_action on every alert since early cycles, but the frontend never rendered it -- a viewer had to click 'View on NVD' and separately look up the CISA KEV catalog to find CISA's actual required remediation text, even though the data was already sitting unused in alerts.json. Added a highlighted .kev-action box (red-tinted border/background, distinct from the neutral CWE/matched-keyword rows) rendered on renderCard() in docs/app.js whenever alert.kev is true AND kev_required_action is present, showing 'CISA required action: <text>' directly on the card. Pure additive frontend change: no new API calls, no backend/schema changes (kev_required_action already existed in the data), zero cost. Validated: node --check passed; served docs/ on a scratch local port (8951) with real production data (501 alerts, 1 KEV entry with a populated kev_required_action), confirmed via browser tool the new box renders the full CISA guidance text correctly, confirmed existing search filter (chrome: 501->110->501 clear) and card layout unaffected, screenshot-confirmed correct visual styling. No aggregate.py/data changes so no data-pipeline dry-run was needed. Live-verified: pushed (frontend-only, no workflow dispatch needed), curled changed live URLs (app.js/style.css/index.html all 200 OK, kev-action string present in app.js), loaded the live dashboard in the browser tool -- confirmed 501/501 alerts, the CVE-2026-85046 KEV card renders the full CISA required-action text correctly styled, screenshot confirmed zero regression to badges, risk bar, CWE row, or card footer.

implemented.title: Extract vendor advisory links from CISA KEV notes field
implemented.description: CISA KEV catalog entries include a notes field (semicolon-separated mix of genuine vendor advisory URLs plus repeated BOD 26-04/Forensics Triage directive boilerplate and a redundant NVD link) that fetch_kev() already retrieves on every run but was never captured or rendered. Added kev_notes to build_final_entry() and the existing-alert refresh loop in scripts/aggregate.py (additive field, null for non-KEV entries, zero new API calls -- parses data already in the KEV catalog response). Added kevNotesLinksHtml() in docs/app.js: splits on ; extracts URLs, filters out nvd.nist.gov/bod-26-04/forensics-triage boilerplate links, and renders remaining genuine advisory links (e.g. vendor security bulletin/release notes) in a new .kev-notes row on the card, placed directly under the existing CISA required-action box. Gives a viewer the vendor patch-notes link without a manual CISA catalog cross-reference.

implemented.title: Show EPSS percentile (relative rank) alongside EPSS score
implemented.description: The pipeline has fetched and stored epss_percentile (each CVE's rank among all EPSS-scored CVEs, a 0-1 fraction) from FIRST.org's EPSS API on every run since early cycles, but it was never rendered anywhere on the dashboard or included in CSV export -- only the raw epss_score probability was shown. Raw EPSS probability and percentile rank answer different questions: a CVE with epss_score=0.02 sounds low in isolation, but if its percentile is 0.98 it is in the top 2% of all scored CVEs by exploitation probability -- a materially different signal for triage prioritization that was previously invisible. Added a small '(top N%)' span next to the EPSS score in each alert card's scores row (docs/app.js renderCard()), computed as 100 - epss_percentile*100, with a title tooltip spelling out the full percentile phrasing; gated on typeof alert.epss_percentile === 'number' so it silently omits for the small number of CVEs missing an EPSS score. Also added epss_percentile as a new column to the CSV export (exportCsv()) immediately after epss_score. Added matching .epss-percentile CSS rule to docs/style.css (small, dim, cursor:help). Pure additive frontend change reading an already-fetched, already-stored field: zero new API calls, zero backend/schema changes, zero cost.

implemented.title: Show CVSS attack-vector/complexity/auth exploitability chip on alert cards
implemented.description: extract_cvss() has always read NVD cvssData.baseScore, but the same cvssData object also carries attackVector/attackComplexity/privilegesRequired/userInteraction -- these were fetched on every run but never parsed or rendered, even though they answer a distinct triage question from the raw score: two CVEs with an identical CVSS 7.5 base score can differ enormously in real-world exploitability (e.g. NETWORK/no-auth/no-interaction vs LOCAL/HIGH-complexity/auth-required). Added extract_cvss_vector_components() to scripts/aggregate.py (NVD v3.1/v3.0 schema only for now; GHSA/Dependabot advisories expose a mixed v3/v4 vector_string without pre-split fields, deferred to a future cycle rather than risking a mis-parse), wired into the NVD candidate dict and build_final_entry() as a new cvss_vector_components field (null for non-NVD-sourced or pre-existing unrefreshed alerts). Frontend renders a compact .exploit-chip badge (e.g. "Network - no auth/interaction") next to CVSS/EPSS in the scores row, with a full-vector tooltip; gated on vc.attack_vector being present so it silently omits where absent. Zero new API calls (parses data already in the existing NVD fetch response).

implemented.title: GHSA/Dependabot CVSS vector component extraction
implemented.description: Parses the CVSS v3.0/v3.1 vector_string field already returned by the GHSA advisories and Dependabot alerts APIs into the same attack_vector/attack_complexity/privileges_required/user_interaction shape NVD-sourced alerts have had since cycle 30, using the fixed public FIRST.org CVSS v3.x abbreviation scheme. CVSS v4.0 vector strings are explicitly detected and skipped (different schema) rather than guessed. No frontend change needed since renderCard() already renders cvss_vector_components generically for any source. implemented.title: Retry/rebase-on-race for aggregator data commit push
implemented.description: The 2026-09-10T00:13 scheduled run failed at the 'Commit and push data changes' step with 'failed to push some refs' -- a non-fast-forward rejection, almost certainly a race between the scheduled run and a manual workflow_dispatch run (or two overlapping scheduled runs) both trying to push updated data/history files to main at nearly the same time. implemented.title: Concurrency guard on aggregation workflow
implemented.description: cve-alerts.yml had no concurrency control -- a scheduled run overlapping with a manual workflow_dispatch (or two dispatches) would double up every NVD/EPSS/KEV/Dependabot/GHSA API call for no benefit, needlessly increasing 429/throttle risk on shared free-tier sources, relying entirely on the existing git-push retry-with-rebase loop to avoid a lost/duplicated commit. Added concurrency: {group: cve-aggregation, cancel-in-progress: false} so overlapping triggers queue rather than race; cancel-in-progress is false so an in-flight run that already fetched/committed data is never killed mid-write.
